With `await page.goto('/photos')` removed, this line now waits for network idle while the page is still `about:blank`, so it is a no-op (and the only reason `page` is destructured). Every test navigates itself, so either drop this line or move the wait after the per-test `page.goto(...)`.

Also, the removed `initially shows a loading spinner` test was the only coverage of the loading state. If it became unreliable because asset requests are now served by the service worker (`page.route` cannot intercept SW fetches), consider re-adding the assertion as a component test on `PhotoViewer` (asserting the spinner while the image has not loaded) instead of dropping the coverage entirely.

Two gaps with cancelling only in the action's `destroy`:

1. The action has no `update`, so when `url` changes on a reused instance (non-keyed `{#each}`, filtered/re-sorted lists) the request for the previous URL is never cancelled and only the latest URL is cancelled at teardown.
2. `cancelImageUrl` is URL-scoped (the service worker tracks pending requests per URL), so if the same thumbnail URL is rendered by more than one mounted component (e.g. a person/album thumbnail in both a grid and a modal/panel), unmounting one instance aborts the request the surviving consumer is still using, which will render as `BrokenAsset`.

Using an `$effect` with the URL captured in the closure handles teardown *and* URL changes, and is more idiomatic in Svelte 5 than returning `destroy` from the mount action:

Cache entries are keyed only by URL (`cache.match(url)` / `cache.put(url, ...)`) and there is no user/session scoping and no purge on logout (`handleLogout()` in `$lib/utils/auth.ts` only resets stores). Because a hit returns before the request reaches the server, media cached by user A stays readable after logging out and logging in as user B on the same browser profile — an authorization/privacy bypass for photos. Consider including a user/session identifier in the cache key (or a per-user cache name) and clearing the asset cache on logout via the same BroadcastChannel.

comments.content: Race condition on `pendingLoads`: two concurrent requests for the same URL each start a network fetch (no in-flight de-duplication), and the second `set()` overwrites the first controller. When `cancel` arrives only the newest load is aborted, and the first load's `finally` then deletes the entry, losing the cancellation handle for the newer load. Check/reuse a pending entry before fetching, and only delete it if it still belongs to this load.
